issue.title: bob-cli PTY transcript test can miss the 87/235 dependencies frame
issue.description: Repository bobs-org/bob-cli, opened through /sase_repo. Deduplicated follow-up from sase-1rq.3.1.1 and sase-1rq.3.1.2; not caused by their changes. Make the PTY transcript fixture deterministic about observing a progress frame: synchronize the producer with rendered output or assert the appropriate stable parser/history contract while retaining real PTY rendering and chatter-suppression coverage. Avoid increasing arbitrary sleeps or weakening production redraw behavior. Scope is small: one test fixture and its assertion timing, with a known 80 ms versus 100 ms scheduling mismatch. Verify repeated serial runs and check-scripts, preserving meaningful phase/order coverage. No quarantine was applied. The independent optional macOS build-time proposal is not part of this task.

task_type_fields.evidence: Proposed independently by sase-1rq.3.1.1 note #1 and sase-1rq.3.1.2 note #1. Both observed StopIteration finding the compiling dependencies 87/235 spinner frame, including on clean baseline dbd30ec0; .1 reports the full suite failed identically with CARGO_INCREMENTAL set and unset. Landing audit on 2026-11-07: six serial passes on current master 63836395 (1.932-1.957 s) and two serial passes (1.946/1.936 s) using untouched scripts/lib exported with git archive from the same baseline dbd30ec0. Thus the earlier failure is not a deterministic regression from the CI fixes. Current local failure rate 0/8; historical failure count/rate beyond the two independent reporter sessions is unknown. CI lint also passed first attempt on 41a2de71 and 63836395. Source lead: test_live.py emits the required counter then changes phase after 0.08 s, while live.py draw skips frames within 0.1 s and selector polls at 0.1 s. That required transient frame is not guaranteed by the renderer contract.

issue.creation_reason: Two CI-repair phase agents reported the same baseline failure; landing reruns on that unchanged baseline passed, confirming an unrelated timing-sensitive test that deserves one follow-up.
